Commentary.Commentary: Shifting focus - Well, the series winner might already be decided, but with the Women's T20 World Cup on the horizon, both teams will still be looking to win the remaining two games. For the 4th T20I, we stay in Johannesburg and the match will be played on Saturday, 25 April. The match will begin at 9.30 pm IST (4 pm GMT), but you can tune in to our build-up a lot sooner. Cheers!

POTM - Laura Wolvaardt! The award goes to South Africa Women's skipper, Laura Wolvaardt, for her match-winning knock of 115 runs off 53 balls. Laura says that it was a lot of fun out there and they knew the importance of getting a strong start while chasing 190. Adds that the wicket played really well in the second innings, which allowed them to keep the momentum going after the Powerplay, and she was pleased to bat through the innings. Mentions that she sensed very early it was a good surface, with the ball coming onto the bat nicely, and adds that getting 70-odd in the Powerplay, with Sune also batting well, set things up perfectly. Shares that the communication with Luus in the middle was all about staying calm and backing their approach. Tells that putting up 70-odd in the Powerplay is still relatively new territory for them, but the message remained simple - keep pushing, trust the firepower in the dugout, and it paid off. Further adds that the team is in a really good space at the moment, with both batting and bowling coming together nicely, and they are improving with each game. Says that chasing has worked in their favour on good surfaces, but they are also mindful of putting up strong totals when batting first, which makes a long series like this valuable. Admits that with the series already secured and the World Cup in mind, there could be a couple of changes in the remaining games. Concludes by saying she is really proud of the group for clinching the series.
... The Presentation ceremony ...

Recapping the first innings - With a bit of rain and lightning around, the start of the game was delayed by half an hour, but once things got underway, it was high-octane action. Having been put into bat, India Women started well and Smriti Mandhana found her timing before falling for 37. Shafali Verma did struggle a bit but fought her way through to notch up yet another half-century. Nonkululeko Mlaba was South Africa's double wicket-taker in the first 10 overs. In the next 10 overs, it was Harmanpreet Kaur who took charge, going on to hammer 66 off just 38 balls and a breezy cameo from Richa Ghosh at the death took India to a massive score of 192/4 in 20 overs. For the Proteas, they used seven bowlers and Annerie Dercksen was the most economical as Mlaba picked up a couple of wickets.

A morale-depleting loss - After a couple of under-par totals in the first two games, India Women finally managed to fire with the bat as they put up 192 runs on the board. However, the bowling was yet again a letdown, and the pacers didn't start well at all. Too many extras and too many boundary balls only added to more misery. The Indian spinners, generally revered for their magic in the middle phase, didn't have a very positive outing either. There were a few dropped catches as well, along with some misfields, which means the reigning ODI Champions need to pull up their socks and end this series on a positive note because they have the individual talent, it just hasn't come off in this series so far.

An all-time great run chase - With 193 needed for the win, it was set up to be an exciting run chase no matter what, but the hosts hardly broke a sweat, gunning it down inside 17 overs. Laura Wolvaardt was the chief architect of the run chase, notching up her 3rd T20I century as well, and this one was the fastest one by a South Africa Women player in the format. At the other end, Sune Luus played a perfect support role but she too racked up the runs, sweeping brilliantly against the spinners and she even hit the winning six. Wolvaardt did get out on 115 with just 10 runs to win, but Luus stayed unbeaten on 64 off 42 balls to seal a memorable win.

Sealing the series in style - What a chase that was! It seemed like even if Indian Women had 250 on the board, Laura Wolvaardt and South Africa Women would have chased it down. It was the sheer intent of the Proteas Women skipper, coupled with her immaculate timing, that blew the opposition away tonight. The hosts take an unassailable 3-0 lead in this five-match T20I series.
